```{python}
from pathlib import Path
import duckdb
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from uk_address_matcher import (
    AddressMatcher,
    ExactMatchStage,
    PeeledAddressStage,
    UniqueTrigramStage,
    SplinkStage,
)

from rent_project.config import (
    DATA_DIRECTORY,
    ADDRESSBASE_DIRECTORY_INTERIM,
    LONDON_BOROUGHS,
)

```

# Compare AddressBase totals to official sources

Comparisons

Local authority level

Council Tax 2011, 2021, 2026: CTSOP1.1 number of properties by Council Tax band, local authority and lower and middle super output area at 31 March 2026

MHCLG Dwelling stock estimates (Live Table 125)

Census: KS401EW Dwellings, household spaces and accommodation type, local authorities in England and Wales

Detailed
Census 2011: QS417EW Household spaces; QS418EW Dwellings; (QS101EW Residence type?)
Census 2021: RM204 Number of Dwellings

```{python}
# My AddressBase spine
spine = pd.read_parquet(
    ADDRESSBASE_DIRECTORY_INTERIM / "greater_london_abplus_spine.parquet"
)

# Council Tax Stock of Properties 
ctsop_2011 = pd.read_csv(
    DATA_DIRECTORY / "raw" / "area-housing-data" / "dwelling-numbers" / "ctsop-properties-2011-lsoa-ctsop_1_1.csv",
    usecols=["geography", "ecode", "area_name", "all_properties"])
ctsop_2011 = (
    ctsop_2011[ctsop_2011["geography"] == "LAUA"][["ecode", "all_properties"]]
    .rename(columns={"ecode": "lad_cd", "all_properties": "ctsop"})
)

ctsop_2021 = pd.read_csv(
    DATA_DIRECTORY / "raw" / "area-housing-data" / "dwelling-numbers" / "ctsop-properties-2021-lsoa-ctsop_1_1.csv",
    usecols=["geography", "ecode", "area_name", "all_properties"])
ctsop_2021 = (
    ctsop_2021[ctsop_2021["geography"] == "LAUA"][["ecode", "all_properties"]]
    .rename(columns={"ecode": "lad_cd", "all_properties": "ctsop"})
)

ctsop_2026 = pd.read_csv(
    DATA_DIRECTORY / "raw" / "area-housing-data" / "dwelling-numbers" / "ctsop-properties-2026-lsoa-ctsop_1_1.csv",
    usecols=["geography", "ecode", "area_name", "all_properties"])
ctsop_2026 = (
    ctsop_2026[ctsop_2026["geography"] == "LAUA"][["ecode", "all_properties"]]
    .rename(columns={"ecode": "lad_cd", "all_properties": "ctsop"})
)

```

```{python}
# need to add status condition (2 or 3 on NA) !!!!!!!!
dwellings_2011 = (
    spine[spine["is_residential_2011"]]
    .groupby("lad11cd")
    .size().rename("spine")
    .rename_axis("lad_cd").reset_index()
    .merge(ctsop_2011, on = "lad_cd")
    .assign(year=2011)
)
dwellings_2021 = (
    spine[spine["is_residential_2021"]]
    .groupby("lad21cd")
    .size().rename("spine")
    .rename_axis("lad_cd").reset_index()
    .merge(ctsop_2021, on = "lad_cd")
    .assign(year=2021)
)
dwellings_2026 = (
    spine[spine["is_residential_2026"]]
    .groupby("lad21cd")
    .size().rename("spine")
    .rename_axis("lad_cd").reset_index()
    .merge(ctsop_2026, on = "lad_cd")
    .assign(year=2026)
)

dwellings = pd.concat(
    [dwellings_2011, dwellings_2021, dwellings_2026],
    ignore_index=True
)
dwellings_long = dwellings.melt(
    id_vars=["lad_cd", "year"],
    value_vars=["spine", "ctsop"],
    var_name="source",
    value_name="dwellings",
)
dwellings_long["borough"] = dwellings_long["lad_cd"].map(LONDON_BOROUGHS)
```


```{python}
g = sns.relplot(
    data=dwellings_long,
    x="year", y="dwellings",
    hue="source", style="source", markers=True, dashes=False,
    col="borough", col_wrap=6,
    kind="line",
    height=2.2, aspect=1.2,
    facet_kws={"sharey": True},
)
g.set(xticks=[2011, 2021, 2026])
g.set_titles("{col_name}", size=9)
g.set_axis_labels("", "Dwellings")
plt.show()
```

# Test HASP to AddressBase Links


Try UK Address Matcher

```{python}
ADDRESS_COLUMNS = ['address_1', 'address_2', 'address_3', 'address_4', 'address_5', 'address_6']

spine = pd.read_parquet(ADDRESSBASE_DIRECTORY_INTERIM / "greater_london_abplus_spine.parquet")

addresses = pd.read_parquet(ADDRESSBASE_DIRECTORY_INTERIM / "greater_london_abplus_addresses.parquet")

rent_properties = pd.read_parquet(DATA_DIRECTORY / "raw" / "hasp-whenfresh-zoopla" / "wfz_rent_properties.parquet")


# preparing address to match
out = None
for col in ADDRESS_COLUMNS:
    s = rent_properties[col].astype('string')
    if out is None:
        out = s
    else:
        out = out.str.cat(s, sep=', ').fillna(out).fillna(s)
rent_properties['address'] = out.fillna('')
del out, s

# matcher
con = duckdb.connect()

hasp_addresses = con.from_df(
    rent_properties[["property_id","address","postcode"]]
    .rename(columns={"property_id": "unique_id", "address": "address_concat"})
)

addressbase_addresses = con.from_df(
    addresses[["uprn","address","postcode"]]
    .rename(columns={"uprn": "unique_id", "address": "address_concat"})
)

matcher = AddressMatcher(
    canonical_addresses=addressbase_addresses,
    addresses_to_match=hasp_addresses,
    con=con,
    stages=[
        ExactMatchStage(),
        PeeledAddressStage(),
        UniqueTrigramStage(),
        # SplinkStage(
        #    # recommended 10.0
        #    final_match_weight_threshold=10, 
        #    # recommended 1.0; initial testing: >2.0
        #    final_distinguishability_threshold=2.1, 
        #),
    ],
)
result = matcher.match()
rent_properties_matched = (
    result.matches().to_df()
    .rename(columns={
        "resolved_canonical_id": "uprn",
        "unique_id": "hasp_property_id"
    })
)

# PRECAUTIONS
# drop all unmatched
rent_properties_matched = rent_properties_matched.dropna(subset=["uprn"])
# drop repeated uprns (all instances)
rent_properties_matched = rent_properties_matched[
    ~rent_properties_matched.duplicated("uprn", keep=False)
]
# 655136 - 2489 - 2501 = 650146


# LAST STEP

# Merging the hasp property id to addresses spine
spine_hasp = spine.merge(
    rent_properties_matched[["hasp_property_id","uprn"]],
    how='left', on="uprn")
# make sure to add a check that spine has not gotten longer
# 4151457 to 4159941, due to uprn duplicates in hasp
# stays 4151457 after dropping uprn duplicates in hasp

# These checks should defo be included in some output, maybe by borough:
len(spine_hasp[~spine_hasp["hasp_property_id"].isna()])
# 650146 as expected
len(spine_hasp[~spine_hasp["hasp_property_id"].isna()]) / len(spine_hasp)
# 16% properties has hasp_property_id
```

INVESTIGATIONS

```{python}

# investigate matches
print(result.match_metrics())
# probabilistic: 49901 unmatched,  685502 matched
# without probabilistic: 80267 unmatched, 655136 matched

# length
len(rent_properties_matched["hasp_property_id"]) # 735403

# no hasp id duplicates
print(rent_properties_matched["hasp_property_id"].nunique()) # 735403
sum(rent_properties_matched["hasp_property_id"].duplicated()) # 0

# number of unmatched
sum(rent_properties_matched["uprn"].isna())
# 49901 (probabilistic) / 80267 (no probabilistic)

# repeated uprns
sum(rent_properties_matched["uprn"].dropna().duplicated()) # 8075 / 2501
dupes = rent_properties_matched.dropna(subset=["uprn"])
dupes = dupes[dupes.duplicated("uprn", keep=False)].sort_values("uprn")
print(dupes["uprn"].nunique()) # 7574 repeated uprns / 2489
sum(dupes["uprn"].duplicated()) # 8075 of the extras / 2501

sampled_uprns = (
    dupes["uprn"].drop_duplicates().sample(n=10, random_state=1)
)
dupes_sample = (
    dupes[dupes["uprn"].isin(sampled_uprns)].sort_values("uprn")
)
dupes_sample.to_csv(ADDRESSBASE_DIRECTORY_INTERIM / "matched_uprn_duplicates_sample_inspection.csv", index=False)

# probabilistic matching
matched_probabilistic_sample = (
    rent_properties_matched[
        rent_properties_matched["match_reason"] == "splink: probabilistic match"
        ]
    .sample(n=20, random_state=1)
)
matched_probabilistic_sample.to_csv(ADDRESSBASE_DIRECTORY_INTERIM / "matched_hasp_to_ab_probabilistic_sample_inspection.csv")

```
